note: Held-out MAE in seconds (lower = better). The research models were trained on the same 540-train / 134-validation athlete split, using a sequence of per-run summary features. The deployed model is a separate LinearRegression on 9 hand-crafted athlete-level aggregates — the features the website can actually collect from a user.

models.name: LinearRegression
models.input: 9 hand-crafted athlete aggregates (pace, weekly mileage, longest run, HR, gender)
models.blurb: The live model. Instant, no heavy dependencies — serves every prediction by default.

models.name: HistoryModel (PyTorch)
models.input: sequence of up to 30 per-run summary vectors (10 features each)
models.blurb: Per-run MLP encoder -> masked mean-pool -> MLP head. Best held-out accuracy. Loaded on demand (torch is imported only when you pick this model), so the first request is slow (cold start).

models.name: GradientBoosting
models.input: per-athlete mean of the 10 per-run features
models.blurb: Tree ensemble on run-mean features. Overfit the small athlete count here.

models.name: Ridge
models.input: per-athlete mean of the 10 per-run features
